estate_courtyard.label: Inner courtyard of the Travancore estate house
estate_courtyard.anchor: The inner courtyard of an old Travancore noble house: sloping tiled roofs on carved timber pillars around it, laterite and lime walls, and a ring of old stones set into the floor. A great jackfruit tree stands over a worn stone platform, with a pyre of stacked mango wood beneath its branches and the dead mistress's long walking stick leaning alone against the trunk.
estate_courtyard.absent: No living Padmini and no hand on the walking stick; no visible face on the shrouded body. No chairs, glass lanterns, coats or uniforms at the rites.
estate_courtyard.time: first light after the rains, pale sky and wet leaves

estate_verandah.label: Verandah of the estate house
estate_verandah.anchor: The verandah of the same Travancore estate house: a raised floor under deep tiled eaves on timber posts, a low writing desk with palm leaves and an iron stylus, and a short flight of steps where a tax collector waits with his palm-leaf bundle.
estate_verandah.absent: No paper, ink bottles, quills or chairs; no Padmini, and no hand but Nagoji's guiding the child's.

war_hall.label: Travancore war hall
war_hall.anchor: Marthanda Varma's war hall: timber pillars, laterite walls with shuttered wooden windows and a sloping tiled roof. A broad low table carries a large hand-drawn map of the coast in ink washes and hatching, with Ramayyan's palm-leaf bundles and stylus at its end; anyone seated sits on a floor mat.
war_hall.absent: No throne, European chairs or glass lamps. No writing, letters, numerals or compass rose on the map, only washes, hatching and tiny drawn hulls; no turban, crest or headband on Varma here.

march_road.label: Laterite road into the Kottarakkara hills
march_road.anchor: A red laterite road winding up into green wooded hills inland, paddy in the valley below. A Travancore column of Nair musketeers in white with cross-belts and matchlocks marches in file with bullock carts behind, and on a far hill stand the steep tiled roofs of an old palace.
march_road.absent: No blue or red coats on any soldier, no stone castle or bastioned fort, no coast or sea, no lettered flags.

siege_lines.label: Siege lines below the Kottarakkara hill town
siege_lines.anchor: The plain below the besieged hill town: a road blocked with felled palms, a canal dammed with packed earth and a raised earthen bund where officers stand. Merchant carts are turned back by Nair sentries while supply carts roll toward the siege lines, and on the hill beyond the old palace's tiled roofs are ringed by the first siege fires.
siege_lines.absent: No town walls, ramparts, ladders or breach; no cannon batteries, blue coats or red coats; no bodies or blood.
siege_lines.time: dusk, siege fires on the hill

velinadu_verandah.label: Verandah of Revathi's house at Velinadu
velinadu_verandah.anchor: The verandah of Revathi's house at Velinadu: low timber pillars, sloping tiled eaves and a polished dark floor, lit only by one brass oil lamp with open wicks. Beyond the eaves lie a dark garden and palms.
velinadu_verandah.absent: No other figures, no glass lamps, no chairs, no war hall map.

palace_approach.label: Old palace of Kottarakkara on its hill
palace_approach.anchor: The old palace of Kottarakkara on its hill: steep tiled roofs over timber upper storeys and laterite walls, its great timber gate braced shut. A path climbs from the plain, where Travancore siege fires ring the foot of the hill.
palace_approach.absent: No stone castle, battlements, gateway tower or foreign fort; no lettered flag, and the white cloth tied to the spear-shaft is blank.

palace_hall.label: Pillared hall of the Kottarakkara palace
palace_hall.anchor: Inside the old palace: a pillared hall of dark carved timber with a polished dark floor, great doors braced with timber beams and a small wicket gate in them, and a wooden-barred window looking down over the plain. A house shrine opens off the hall, its tall brass standing lamp burning with open wicks.
palace_hall.absent: No throne, chairs, glass lamps or European furniture; no uniforms on Savitri's retainers, who wear plain mundus and carry spears.
palace_hall.time: dusk into night, brass oil lamps

paddy_battlefield.label: Trampled paddy field near Kottarakkara
paddy_battlefield.anchor: A field of trampled paddy between low bunds, ringed by coconut palms, with a small roadside shrine half hidden in the palms and a canal road leading west into them. Savitri's force are local men in mundus with flintlocks and spears under a plain cloth banner; the Travancore musketeers are Nair men in white with cross-belts and matchlocks.
paddy_battlefield.absent: No shore, sea or ships; no blood, bodies or gore; no blue or red coats on any soldier; the banner has a painted emblem and no writing.

kings_tent.label: The king's tent at the edge of the field
kings_tent.anchor: Marthanda Varma's campaign tent at the edge of the battlefield: heavy cream cotton canvas on timber poles, the flap tied open on the field, woven mats and a low cushioned seat, his spear leaning on the tent pole. Nair guards in white mundu with spears stand at the flap.
kings_tent.absent: No throne, European chairs, camp tables or glass lanterns; no map or writing; no blood on Savitri, only the darkening bruise.

exile_path.label: Path west through the palms
exile_path.anchor: A path running west from the camp through coconut palms past burned fields, smoke drifting across the evening sky and mixing with a pale band of sea haze at the very edge of the horizon.
exile_path.absent: No ships, boats, shore or open sea in view; no chains on Savitri, only her bound hands; no blood.

character_notes.nagoji: Thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and jaw with no beard or facial scar, and a tiny flush gold ear stud on the lobe with nothing hanging from it. Kerala topknot, no turban or hat, black hair with only the first grey at the temples; in the war hall, on campaign and at Kottarakkara he wears the uniform of white coat, red waistcoat, brass buttons and silver chain over the coat, and at Padmini's funeral on page 1 he is bare-chested in a plain white mundu with no border, the forearm brand turned from camera.
character_notes.temple_priest: The V13 temple priest face, used here only for the Hindu funeral priest at Padmini's rites: sacred thread and ash marks on the forehead. Never Ramayyan's face or a bearer's.
character_notes.nandini: A small girl of about six, Padmini's sister's daughter and heir, with no character sheet: keep the same round child's face, dark hair and plain white cotton in both of her panels.
character_notes.revathi: A little younger than Nagoji, wearing a tali, with grey threading at the temples that her sheet lacks. At Padmini's funeral on page 1 she wears plain borderless white with no jasmine and no gold except the tali; on the Velinadu verandah on page 4 she wears her indigo sari with gold, the flat-coin necklace and jasmine in her braid.
character_notes.ramayyan: Thin sharp fine features and receding hair, plain unbordered white cloth, palm-leaf bundles and an iron stylus. No forehead marks or sacred thread, never the funeral priest's face.
character_notes.varma: Face, moustache and build from his sheet with black hair, never the grey of the sheet's later figure; in the war hall on pages 2 to 4 he is bare-headed with his hair in a side knot above the LEFT ear, no turban, crest or headband, bare-chested in cream and gold with gold necklaces. In the king's tent on pages 8 and 9 he wears the campaign look: cream-and-gold turban with the jewelled peacock-feather crest, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth and gold necklaces.
character_notes.eustachius: Tall, a head above Nagoji, clean-shaven, with pale hair going grey. A plain white Travancore coat with no red waistcoat, never a blue coat or tricorne.
character_notes.savitri: About fifty, a lean face with lines of care at the eyes and mouth, her black hair streaked with grey in a low knot at the nape, older and greyer than her sheet. Plain white mundu and neriyathu with no border in the old Kerala drape with no stitched blouse, no jasmine and no jewellery, whatever the sheet's blouse and sari drape show.
